findings.evidence: In the proof, `g` appears only inside `hgu`, and `hgu` is used only through `ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable hK`. The bound itself is `opNNNorm_comp_le` composed with `hC`.
findings.fix: State the bound for general operators: `{A : E → F →L[ℝ] G} (hA : AEStronglyMeasurable A μ) (hC : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖A x‖₊ ≤ C) : eLpNorm (fun x => (A x).comp (Du x)) p μ ≤ C * eLpNorm Du p μ`, with no measurability assumption on `K`. Then apply it to `A = fderiv ℝ g ∘ u` and `μ.restrict K` at the call sites, and give it a name that is not about `fderiv`.
findings.issue: `eLpNorm_fderiv_comp_le` is stated for `fderiv ℝ g (u x)` and assumes `ContinuousOn` on a `MeasurableSet K`. The proof uses neither `g` nor continuity, except to get measurability via `aestronglyMeasurable_fderiv_comp`. The same over-specialization appears in the private helpers `aestronglyMeasurable_fderiv_comp` (line 86) and `memLp_fderiv_comp` (line 113).

findings.evidence: `hT : IsCompact (cthickening η (u '' S)) := huS.cthickening` is the only step that needs F to be proper. The mollification and the `L¹` steps all happen in `E`, not `F`.
findings.fix: Drop `FiniteDimensional ℝ F` and keep only `CompleteSpace F`, which `hu.completeSpace` already provides. Get the uniform convergence of `g ∘ un` and `Dg ∘ un` from continuity of `g` and `fderiv ℝ g` on the compact set `u '' S` (a Lebesgue-number argument) instead of from compactness of a thickening.
findings.issue: `[FiniteDimensional ℝ F]` is assumed by `HasWeakFDerivOn.comp_contDiffOn` and everything downstream, including `MemWkpLoc.comp_contDiffOn` and both `comp_graph` forms. It is used only to make `cthickening η (u '' S)` compact so that Heine–Cantor applies. The weak chain rule for continuous `u` holds for any Banach `F`: uniform convergence `un → u` into a compact image inside the open set `W` already makes `g ∘ un → g ∘ u` and `Dg ∘ un → Dg ∘ u` uniform on `V`.

summary: The chain-rule statements are at the right level, but the public local bound is tied to `fderiv ℝ g (u x)` and assumes continuity when it only needs a measurable, a.e.-bounded family of operators. The core section also adds a `FiniteDimensional ℝ F` assumption that only serves the proof.
